Subject: Recap + Next Steps: Performance SLOs & Multi-region Routing (US/EU/APAC)

Hi Samir / Claire —

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap of what we heard and proposed next steps so we’re aligned before the technical workshop:

Summary of customer requirements (as discussed)
- Latency targets: p95 <= 150ms (hard target), p50 ~60ms (desired). Some endpoints will accept up to 200ms p95 for larger context scoring.
- Throughput: baseline 2k req/min, spiky 10k req/min with autoscale burst.
- Concurrency: sustained ~50 concurrent scoring sessions; peak concurrency ~200 for business hours spike.
- Streaming: most scoring calls need streaming token-by-token output (low initial token latency, partial results for UI). WebSocket or chunked HTTP streaming preferred.
- Multi-region: traffic must be routed to closest region (US, EU, APAC) with < 100ms RTT goal for regional users; cross-region failover acceptable but should notify and degrade gracefully.
- Data residency: EU customer data must remain in EU region (processing + logs). APAC customers likewise prefer APAC residency.

What Redwood proposes (high level)
- Regional dedicated pools: provisioned dedicated GPUs per region with smart routing and automatic fallback to a secondary region if a regional pool is saturated.
- Autoscaling + burst: config to meet baseline and spike requirements; we recommend autoscale with burst capacity and short warm pools for streaming-heavy endpoints.
- Streaming support: continuous streaming with 40–60ms per-token generation on optimized serving path for the model class we discussed.
- SLO enforcement & monitoring: per-route p95/p50 dashboards, tracing hooks, and alerts tied to your QA prompt sets.
- Data residency controls: customer can pin a workload to EU/APAC region; logs and audit trails can be configured to stay within the region and integrate with your KMS/HSM.

Open questions (please confirm):
1) Are the throughput numbers above (2k baseline / 10k spike) per product or per account?
2) For streaming, do you require server-initiated partial results via a persistent socket, or is HTTP chunked streaming sufficient for the UI?
3) Any regulatory constraints around backup/replication windows for EU data?

Attachments: slo-matrix.xlsx (proposed SLO matrix + config), redwood-arch.pdf (regional routing + high-level infra).

Next steps
- Confirm answers to the questions above.
- Technical workshop: propose Wed 18 Mar or Thu 19 Mar — 30–45 mins with your infra/security + our infra lead (Rishi). Book here: https://cal.redwood.ai/marissa/finova-tech-workshop
- We’ll share a short POC plan and SOC2 summary ahead of the workshop.

If that looks right I’ll send a calendar invite and include our infra and security SMEs.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Senior Sales Engineer
Redwood Inference

+1 (415) 555-0123

Thanks Marissa — quick clarifications from our side.

- Throughput: the 2k/10k numbers are per product (we have two primary products, but will likely ramp one first). For the initial POC we expect ~1.5k baseline, 6k spike.
- Streaming: WebSocket would be preferred for the UI team (they want minimal latency on first byte and the ability to cancel mid-stream). HTTP chunked streaming is acceptable as fallback.
- Data residency: EU residency is mandatory for EU customers (processing + logs). For APAC we have a preference but can be flexible if latency is problematic.

Can you also confirm whether Redwood supports customer-managed KMS for encryption keys and whether you maintain a SOC 2 report we can share with procurement?

Samir

Hi Samir — good data, thanks. A few clarifications from our tech side: 

- Throughput for POC: we’ll size the EU pool for 1.5k baseline / 6k spike per product as requested. We’ll include headroom for two products in the sizing doc.
- WebSocket streaming: supported — our runtime supports both WebSocket and chunked HTTP streaming. WebSocket gives lower first-byte latency and easier mid-stream cancellation. We’ll include a short sample client for your frontend team.
- Customer-managed KMS: yes, we support integration with customer KMS (AWS KMS + external HSM via KMIP) for key wrapping of long-term logs and backups.
- SOC 2: we maintain a SOC 2 Type II report; will share an executive summary ahead of the workshop.

Proposed technical workshop participants from Redwood: Rishi (infra lead), Ethan (runtime engineer), myself. From Finova: Samir + your infra/security lead + a frontend engineer for streaming details.

I’ll send a calendar invite for Wed 18 Mar 11:00–11:45 UTC unless you prefer Thu. If that works I’ll attach the POC plan and a proposed rollout timeline (POC -> pilot -> production).

Best,
Marissa

Claire / Samir — great, thanks for the clarifications. Action items and answers below: 

Answers:
- Data residency: we support region-scoped workloads. For EU workloads we will pin processing and logs to the EU region for the POC and production. Any cross-region replication will require a written change request and contractual approval.
- KMS: customer-managed KMS supported (AWS KMS + external HSM via KMIP). We encrypt logs and backups and can arrange key wrapping so Redwood never has access to raw key material.
- SOC 2: attaching an executive summary (SOC2-summary.pdf). Full SOC 2 report available under NDA / secure link.
- POC timeline & cost: typical POC (POC -> pilot -> production) is 6–8 weeks. For the POC we estimate a dedicated EU pool sized for 1.5k baseline / 6k spike at ~$8k–12k/month (depending on GPU sizing and burst policy). We’ll provide a detailed cost estimate in the POC plan.
